messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/credits: if a customer switches plans mid-cycle what exactly persists vs resets? :question:

matt: TL;DR: quotas/rate-limits reflect the active plan; credits (promo, one-offs) stay on the account until used/expired.

sophia: To add: upgrading gives you immediate quota increases for new allocations, but we don't scale promo credits to match the new plan.

elaine: What about outage buffers we apply as relief? If they move to Dedicated, does the buffer move too?
matt: Yes—buffers are tied to account_id and follow across plan changes until TTL expiry. They're stored as metadata on the billing bucket.

sam: Finance: consumed credits aren't reclaimed when downgrading. Refunds for unused committed credits are reviewed by finance per contract.

riley: Rate-limit provisioning: when you upgrade, the routing layer enacts new RPS limits after provisioning (typically under 5 minutes). Until then the former limits hold.

elaine: If we fallback to a cheaper model variant during contention, which price applies?
sophia: Billing charges the actual model variant that served the request. We log model_id in traces and billing breakdowns.

andre: Safety note: if fallthrough changes unit price by >10% we emit an account event and a billing note; customers can opt into stricter no-fallback policies.

elaine: Streaming billing: if a stream is cut mid-response, how do we meter tokens?
riley: We meter at flush points. Tokens flushed before the cut are billed. We include headers like X-Stream-Flushed-Tokens and X-RateLimit-Remaining. Example:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 150
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 48
X-Stream-Flushed-Tokens: 980
```

sam: Partial-stream charges deduct from account credits; refunds require manual adjustments.

elaine: Launch-day spikes—what's the temporary quota increase flow?
sophia: Self-serve UI in Console coming mid-May. Until then, open a support request with the "quota-increase" tag and include RPS and duration. Example payload recommended in support note.
matt: Ops SLA: requests with telemetry usually processed within 24h; multi-region requests may take 48h.

elaine: Do our managed health probes count against customer quotas?
riley: No—managed probes from our health-check IPs using agent keys are excluded. Customer-originated pings do count; suggest using low-cost monitoring endpoints.

andre: For load testing we can provision test buckets isolated from production credits—contact support to provision.

elaine: Any rollout dates?
sophia: Self-serve quota UI: mid-May. Route-level billing visibility (beta): June. Fallthrough >10% alerts: rolling in April. Docs and console banners before launch.

matt: We'll post an FAQ link in the all-hands follow-up. Ping us for customer-specific walkthroughs. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Task created BILL-534: add Console copy + fallthrough event triggers.

elaine: Thanks all, saving thread for notes.
sam: Logging a finance follow-up on refund edge-cases.

and re: andre: I'll own the support playbook for downgrades/refunds.
matt: End thread.
